title: Hear my call, Varuṇa; do not take away our life

words.gram: root aorist imperative, 2nd sg. active (Vedic -dhi, lengthened)

words.meaning: I have called on, I long for
words.context: Bhāskara: «आचके आभिमुख्येन शब्दयामि प्रार्थये», from «कै गै शब्दे»

sandhi.rule: final m before a vowel is kept and joins it

morphology.note: the imperative श्रुधि with the final vowel lengthened in the Saṃhitā; Bhāskara: «'श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्यः' इति धिभावः».
अद्य with its final vowel lengthened in the Saṃhitā of a ṛk.

translation.literal: Hear this call of mine, O Varuṇa, and be gracious today; seeking help, I have called on you.
translation.readable: Varuṇa, hear my call and be gracious to me today: I call on you, seeking your protection.

words.context: Bhāskara: «तत्तदर्थम्», ‘for that purpose’, or «तदेव त्वां यामि याचे»

words.role: main verb of the first clause

words.meaning: with the sacred word, with prayer

words.gram: present middle participle, m. nom. sg.
m. nom. sg. (present middle participle of √यज्)
present middle participle, negated, m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: do not steal, do not take away

sandhi.rule: visarga before t becomes s; t before a vowel becomes d
i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y

morphology.note: the s-aorist of √मुष् without augment, used with the prohibitive मा: ‘do not steal’.
the root-aorist imperative of √बुध्; Bhāskara explains the form at length («'हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः'»).

translation.literal: That I ask of you, praising you with prayer; that the sacrificer hopes for with offerings. Not angry, O Varuṇa, take notice here; O widely praised one, do not steal away our life.
translation.readable: With prayer and praise I come to you for this; the sacrificer asks it with his offerings. Be not angry, Varuṇa: attend to us here, you whose praise is wide, and do not take away our life.

meaning: The first two verses of the evening upasthāna, to Varuṇa, the god of cosmic order who sees and punishes wrongdoing and is approached in the evening. The first is a short cry for help: hear me today and be gracious. The second, a triṣṭubh, asks him not to be angry and not to cut life short. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (2.1.11.6) they are the invitatory and offering verses of a rice-offering to Varuṇa (Bhāskara’s viniyoga); in the Ṛgveda they are 1.25.19 and 1.24.11, from the hymns of Śunaḥśepa — the man saved from being sacrificed, whose story makes them prayers for release.
in_the_rite: Evening sūryopasthāna, recited standing and facing west, followed by yac cid dhi and the two verses after it. The Mylapore prayoga gives the viniyoga for the evening verses: Śunaḥśepa the seer, gāyatrī and triṣṭubh the metres, Varuṇa the deity, used in the upasthāna of the evening Sandhyā (vin-imam-me).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, on TS 2.1.11, gives the use: «अथ 'ये कृष्णास्स्युस्तं वारुणं चरुं निर्वपेत्' इत्यस्याः पुरोनुवाक्या - इमं म इति गायत्री», and «तत्रैव याज्या - तत्त्वेति त्रिष्टुप्».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: On the meaning he stresses that the worshipper asks for protection («अवस्युः रक्षणमात्मन इच्छन्») and, in the second verse, for life: «नः अस्माकं आयुर्दीप्तिमन्नं वा मा प्रमोषीः मा छेत्सीः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The first verse is a gāyatrī, the second a triṣṭubh. The Ṛgveda (1.25.19, 1.24.11) has the same words; the Taittirīya writes इमम्मे and बोद्ध्युरु, and the GRETIL Ṛgveda writes the Vedic ḷ for ḍ (its encoding prints मृऌअय, अहेऌअमानो for मृळय, अहेळमानो).

notes.label: historical
notes.text: Ṛgveda 1.24–30 are ascribed to Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti, whose release from the sacrificial post is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa; the prayoga’s viniyoga names him as the seer.
